findings.original_finding: The stability proof originally said a rejected applicant always leaves the institution holding somebody preferred. An unacceptable applicant may be rejected while the institution remains empty, so that sentence did not cover the stated incomplete-list domain.
findings.requested_correction: Separate rejection of an unacceptable partner, who cannot form a blocking pair, from acceptable-applicant rejection followed by an improving held partner.

proof_audit: Second-price threshold proof covers winning, losing and equality, reserve eligibility and report-independent tie priority. Truthfulness is weak dominance, not a unique best response or a common-value bidding formula.

Uniform first-price derivative has the sign of v-z on the positive imitation domain; zero and A type boundaries, zero bid, support endpoint and all above-support bids are considered. The proof establishes the displayed equilibrium rather than uniqueness.

Revenue identity is derived from both incentive inequalities, monotone X, continuous-X squeeze and the fundamental theorem of calculus. Independence keeps the opponents distribution fixed across own-type comparisons; the boundary utility and distinction between interim and conditional payments are explicit.
The common-value calculation conditions on own H and rival L, not all winning events; tied H signals and the payment rule are explicitly left for a complete bidding calculation.

DA termination, corrected stability and first-achievable-rejection proposer-optimality proofs cover finite strict own-partner preferences with outside options. The first achievable rejection must retain an acceptable alternative; the earlier-rejection contradiction and blocking-pair conclusion are valid.
The general DA proposer strategy-proofness theorem is stated honestly and deferred to v13-c11. It is not inferred merely from proposer optimality or finite tests.

Serial-dictatorship truthfulness follows from report-independent priority and an unchanged available set. Under truthful rankings the earliest-changed-person argument proves one-sided Pareto efficiency. Two-sided stable matchings are Pareto efficient for all participants under strict own-partner preferences, without asserting applicant-only efficiency or cardinal welfare from rank sums.

Fixed compulsory fees preserve the allocation and bidding comparisons but change boundary utility; voluntary entry requires a new analysis. Reserves, correlation, risk aversion, asymmetry and institutional deviations are not assigned universal revenue rankings.
